evidence: Both rows are Eldorado's Northwest Ice Couloir above Marble Creek Cirque (Grade III, ~1,000 ft couloir 7,800-8,800 ft, FA Dan Cauthorn and Bill Pilling), approached by rappelling from the Eldorado/Dean's Spire notch. Keep this row because it carries all the content and the FA; the other is an empty shell. Rename it to 'Northwest Ice Couloir', since 'Eldorado Glacier' is only part of the approach.

This is an empty row (no prose, FA, face or commitment) for the same Eldorado NW Ice Couloir that wa_eldorado_peak_eldorado_glacier_nw fully describes. Fold it into that row, which should take this row's correct name.

Baring's standard route is called the Northwest Ridge: a very steep climbers' trail to the NW ridge crest, then the basin and a gully to the 5,550-ft notch between the south and main peaks, with easy Class 3 just below the summit. This row's beta describes exactly that line, and its face even reads 'Northwest Ridge / South notch'. Keep the Northwest Ridge name and move this row's prose and FA into it after checking them.

content_belongs_to: none: the 'ice' discipline and 'Easy 5th WI1 PG13' grade describe no part of this route

what_this_route_is.overview: A multi-day loop around Mount Adams, not a route to the summit. It links the Round the Mountain, Pacific Crest and Highline trails, and closes the loop with a trailless stretch of about 4-5 miles on the east side ('The Gap'). That stretch crosses the Mazama, Klickitat and Rusk glaciers, unstable moraine and talus, and glacial rivers such as the Big Muddy. The east side lies on Yakama Nation land, which requires a permit and can be closed.

evidence: Sources describe a loop of roughly 35-40 miles with about 8,600 ft of gain, mostly on trail plus an off-trail glacier and moraine section. There is no roped 5th-class rock or graded ice on the normal line. Mountain Project's page lists 'Easy 5th', which this row copied, but trip reports describe non-technical glacier crossing and loose scrambling. Consider re-labeling it as a trek or taking it out of the summit-route list.

The Finger Traverse is the rock alternative to the Terrible Traverse on the standard South Chute route (~7,435 ft), not a separate way to the summit. The standard route is the row wa_mount_constance_north_chimney, whose own overview calls itself the South Chute. Fold this row in as a named option in that route's breakdown. Separately, the parent is misnamed and should be called 'South Chute'.

The Terrible Traverse is part of the standard South Chute route: an exposed snow traverse across a cirque above a big cliff, with the Finger Traverse as its alternative. Fold it into the standard-route row wa_mount_constance_north_chimney (really the South Chute) as one of the two crux options.

what_this_route_is.overview: The line of the 1958 first ascent of West Fury, climbed from the west rather than along the ridge from East Fury. From a camp on the upper Challenger Glacier, the party crossed steep heather and cliffs down to the glacier west of Mount Fury. They then climbed two steep, shallow chimneys on loose rock, working around a chockstone, to gain the west ridge, and a short easy scramble led to the summit. The route is remote and committing, and the first party came down in the dark, rappelling and bivouacking.
what_this_route_is.fa: Vic Josendal, Maury Muzzy, Phil Sharpe, Warren Spickard, R. Duke Watson, August 19, 1958

evidence: The FA field correctly names the 1958 west-side first ascent, but the face, overview and beta (start from East Fury, three towers on the connecting ridge) describe the East Fury-West Fury traverse, which was not completed until later. That content belongs to wa_ridge_traverse_from_east_fury. The crux of the west-side chimneys has no published rating, so 'Class 4' is low confidence.

The guide lists three routes on Lincoln: South Ridge (Class 2, the easiest), Flapjack Lake and North Ridge (Class 3), and Harniss Chute (Class 3). This row's face (South Ridge), its 'easiest way, class 2 per the historic line' beta and its Class 2 breakdown fit the South Ridge, and the Flapjack Lakes name contradicts them. Rename it South Ridge and drop the Flapjack wording, or rewrite the row as the Class 3 Flapjack/North Ridge route if that is what it is meant to be. That route is not in the catalog yet.

The East Face Ramps (Class 4 with one 5th-class step) is one of the summit-block finishes on the Blue Glacier / Crystal Pass standard route; the 5.4 north-side finishes are the others. Its beta repeats the whole Blue Glacier approach. Fold it into wa_mount_olympus_blue_glacier as that route's normal finish rather than keeping a second 'Standard' row. The north and west-edge variation rows can stay as variations.

The Hester Lake Route goes around Little Hester Lake to the ~4,640-ft saddle to its northwest, then follows Price's NORTH Ridge to the summit (Class 3 snow and rock gullies). That makes it the same line as the North Route row. Keep the established Hester Lake Route name. Also fix this row's 'south/east flank ... east ridge' wording to 'north ridge'.

Rahm's standard route is the South Side: from Ouzel Lake, gain the upper terrace, then pass the 7,700-ft cliff band by a hidden ~40-ft Class 4/5 gully (or a longer Class 3 gully to its right) and reach the summit by the upper basin. Both rows describe this one route. Keep 'South Side', which matches the published name and has the precise beta, and move the other row's overview and FA into it.

'Standard Route / Glacier' is the same south-side gully route from Ouzel Lake as wa_mount_rahm_south_side, and its face says so. 'Glacier' is misleading because the line is talus, gullies and a snowfield. Fold it into South Side, keeping its peak overview and its FA (Hutton/Mason 1955, not independently verified).

Both rows are Mount Stone's standard South Couloir: the Putvin Trail to Lake of the Angels, then a skirt west of the cliffs (avoiding St. Peter's Gate) to the summit pinnacle. It is mostly Class 2-3 with one Class 4 step. Mountain Project and the Mountaineers call it 'South Couloir', so keep this row (fuller beta) under that name and fold the Putvin row in.

This row has the same face, approach and crux as wa_mount_stone_lake_of_angels. 'Putvin Trail' is only the approach to the South Couloir. Fold it into the kept row, whose name should become 'South Couloir'.
